title: Kitagawa 2005 Experiment 2 · rear distractors
citation: Kitagawa, N., Zampini, M., & Spence, C. (2005). Audiotactile interactions in near and far space. Experimental Brain Research, 166(3–4), 528–537.
notes: The auditory inspection enumerates all published stimulus cells and needs unbundled burst trains. It omits electrical delivery and the speeded footpedal task.

auditory.source: Rear loudspeaker positions at 20 and 70 cm from head center, at ±45° from the rear axis on each side.

response.task: Speeded discrimination of the earlobe side while ignoring the sound.

analysis.inverse_efficiency: Median correct RT divided by proportion correct within the condition.
analysis.interference: Opposite-side minus same-side inverse efficiency. Exclude incorrect trials and responses absent by 1200 ms from RT analysis.

inspection_scope.details: The software inspection uses a pooled sound-trigger schedule with nominal tactile side and timing annotations. No tactile pulses, pedal input, deliberate feedback or original condition-block order are run.

implementation_gaps: Original sound waveform bytes and acoustic trigger-to-ear timing are unavailable. The unbundled 250 ms WAV input for each condition requires the reported burst train and calibrated physical rear speaker channels.
Software response capture requires a lateral choice and correctness scoring. The auditory schedule is for inspection.

The scheduler requires four independently selected sound-type-by-distance blocks, three calibrated earlobe pulses on the designated channel, a verified 30 ms sound lead, and two footpedals with feedback and scoring.
